title: 'Maestri's Wagons' and the song Nash made about a raid
summary: Nash discusses the song, cannot recall its history or words, then sings a verse he made up after a raid at the boot-life house where he stayed.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: You were talking about this Maestri song that you sang.
Yes, he used to do this song of Maestri's Wagons.
How did that song grow up?
How did you know the history of the song? Do you know the history of the song?
I really sure don't. I know the history of it, but I remember when I was born.
Do you remember any of the words to it?
Well, no, I can't remember the words.
You don't know what it's about or anything like that? Maestri's Wagons?

I sure don't. I know Maestri's Wagons. Of course, all those old tunes like that, you can always learn it if you meet somebody. If you meet somebody that's really familiar with it, I mean, learn it. I know a lot of old songs that I used to do, I forgot all about it. I went to some guys and got the words of it right back.
Well, tell us the history of that, there they go with my jam.
What's the song in some kind of their life?

I used to intern at the Boot Life house. And one night they came in there and they rent this house. And so I told the guy, I said, next day, I'm going to write a song about this, about this rating. He said, what it going to be? I said, this way is going to be. And I started singing it. There they go with my gin, Hiring the world, the day breaking. But all they love was broken by. Well, the last time that they raised that train, I thought that they was through. Well, bad enough that they raised the joint. And came and got the man's wife too. So there they go, full of joy. They break the tumbling like a baby break of joy. But all they left was broken by.
